answer: We formalize a Sybil-resistant mechanism where an agent's opportunity-cost bond B is locked alongside a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function. To prevent identity multiplication, we define a slashing penalty P > B that triggers a cascade across the security ridge. This economic ripple ensures any malicious entity attempting to simulate distinct node identities faces a strictly negative expected payoff. Consequently, the Nash equilibrium converges to honest participation, positioning the honest strategy atop the payoff knoll.
